property_summary: A call to sendTo from a non-owner must always revert; the mutant with require(false) reverts even for the owner, violating this invariant.
A call to sendTo by the owner must not revert; the mutant with require(false) always reverts, even for the owner.
A call to sendTo by any sender must revert ONLY when the caller is not the owner; the reference preserves this, but the mutant with require(false) reverts unconditionally regardless of the sender.

For any sender, if a call to sendTo does not revert, the receiver's balance must increase by exactly the sent amount; the buggy version with require(false) always reverts, so it trivially satisfies this vacuously, but the reference version guarantees actual fund transfer for the owner.

For any call where the sender is the owner, the call to sendTo must not revert; the reference lets the owner proceed, but the mutant with require(false) always reverts, even for the owner, breaking this rule.

For any call to sendTo, the ETH balance of the sender (owner) never decreases because the owner is supposed to send to an external receiver, but the mutant sends it back to the owner (msg.sender) which leaves the owner’s balance unchanged; the bug violates this by decreasing the owner's balance when the receiver happens to match msg.sender.
After sendTo(receiver, amount) is called by the owner, the ETH balance of the receiver increases by exactly the transferred amount, but the mutant increases msg.sender's balance instead.

For any call by the owner to sendTo(receiver, amount), the ETH balance of the passed receiver address must increase by exactly `amount`; the mutant instead increases msg.sender's balance, thus failing to increase the receiver's balance.

After a successful sendTo(receiver, amount) call by the owner, the ETH balance of the specified receiver must increase by exactly amount; the mutant instead sends the ETH to msg.sender, so the intended receiver's balance does not increase.

After a successful `sendTo(receiver, amount)` call by the owner, the ETH balance of the `receiver` must increase by exactly `amount`; the mutant sends ETH to `msg.sender` instead, so the receiver's balance does not increase.
After any call to sendTo, the contract must remain alive (i.e., its code size is non-zero); the mutant violates this by self-destructing when the caller is the owner.
For any valid call to sendTo by the owner, the contract's code size must remain non-zero; the mutant selfdestructs, reducing code size to zero.
After any call to sendTo, the contract's ether balance must decrease by exactly the transferred amount; the mutant selfdestructs, sending all balance away and breaking this invariant.
For any call to sendTo by the owner with any receiver and amount, the contract's code size afterwards must remain strictly greater than zero; the mutant selfdestructs, reducing code size to zero.
For any call to sendTo by the owner, the contract's bytecode size after the call must equal its bytecode size before the call; the mutant selfdestructs, making the bytecode size zero afterwards.
After sendTo, the ETH balance of the contract must decrease by the amount sent (i.e., transfer forwards the value); the buggy call-without-value leaves the contract balance unchanged.
After sendTo, the receiver's ETH balance must increase by exactly the sent amount; the bug uses a valueless call so the receiver gets nothing.
The owner can withdraw the contract's entire balance via sendTo; the buggy version using a valueless call leaves the contract balance unchanged despite the owner's instruction to send ETH.
After a successful sendTo called by the owner, the contract's ETH balance must decrease by at least the amount parameter; the buggy version uses a valueless call so the balance never decreases.

For any owner-initiated sendTo, if the receiver is a contract that does not revert, the call must succeed but the receiver's balance must not increase because the call sends no value; the buggy version succeeds without transferring ETH, while the correct transfer reverts due to insufficient balance in C.
